purpose: rank the proteins of a phage genome by probability of being a holin
recipe: HistGradientBoosting over 36 handcrafted features + 480-d mean-pooled ESM-2 (t12_35M). TM-anchored local features were tested and rejected (scripts/15).

honest_performance_leave_one_genome_out.note: Leave-one-genome-out over every annotated holin in a 66-genome panel (scripts/40_logo_benchmark.py, reports/logo_benchmark.json): 53 holins in 50 genomes. For each genome the holin's homologues are removed from training before it is scored. This deployment model trains on everything, so these are the estimate, not its own score.

superseded_small_benchmark.note: Earlier figures from scripts/22 on 13 annotated holins in 16 genomes. Kept for the record; they did not hold up on the larger panel and should not be quoted.

known_limits: profile-match evidence: only 7 of 2,886 curated holins are Swiss-Prot reviewed
Pfam is exhausted as a source: 4,700 of 4,701 curated records joined existing families
P1 lydD remains the weakest annotated holin (0.60, rank 3/110)
the true holin is top-ranked in its genome only 66-70% of the time (in the top 5: 93-98%): use the output as a ranked shortlist
high-confidence cut-off for this model is 0.95 (the endolysin model uses 0.9995; read the per-class high_conf column)
a genuinely novel holin family gets a shortlist, not an answer (strict AP 0.613)
the 66-genome panel resolves differences only above ~0.05 AP
usage: import pickle, features as F; m=pickle.load(open('models/holin_model_curated.pkl','rb')); X=hstack([handcrafted, esm.embed(seqs)]); m['model'].predict_proba(X)[:,1]
